title: Airships and the Future that Never Was

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: They are hulking, but graceful.
sentences.zh: 它们笨重却又优雅。

sentences.en: Human-made whales that float in the air.
sentences.zh: 那是漂浮空中的人造巨鲸。

sentences.en: For over 100 years, lighter-than-air aircraft have fascinated us,
sentences.zh: 一个多世纪以来，轻于空气的飞行器一直让我们着迷，

sentences.en: and they have this recurring, starring role in our dreams of an alternate reality,
sentences.zh: 在我们对平行现实的幻想中，它们反复扮演着主角，

sentences.en: of a future that might have been,
sentences.zh: 幻想那个可能存在过的未来，

sentences.en: where cargo and passengers traverse the globe in a civilized fashion
sentences.zh: 在那个未来里，货物与乘客以文明的方式横跨全球，

sentences.en: and dock elegantly on the mooring towers on top of Art Deco skyscrapers.
sentences.zh: 并优雅地停靠在装饰艺术风格摩天大楼顶部的系泊塔上。

sentences.en: If you've seen one in real life, it was likely a blimp, emblazoned with the Goodyear logo.
sentences.zh: 如果你在现实生活中见过它们，那很可能是一个喷印着固特异标志的气球。

sentences.en: A blimp is a non-rigid airship, meaning that there's no structure inside the balloon.
sentences.zh: 软式飞艇是一种非刚性飞艇，意味着气囊内部没有任何结构。

sentences.en: It's just a balloon.
sentences.zh: 它就是一个气球。

sentences.en: The shape is maintained by the pressure of the lifting gas inside.
sentences.zh: 它的形状靠内部升力气体的压力来维持。

sentences.en: Then you add a little cockpit and engines and rudders on the outside of that big balloon to make it fly.
sentences.zh: 然后你在那个大气球的外部加上一个小驾驶舱、发动机和方向舵，让它飞起来。

sentences.en: Today's blimps are basically cute PR novelties,
sentences.zh: 如今的软式飞艇基本上是可爱的公关新奇玩意，

sentences.en: but for around 100 years, lighter-than-air aircraft were seriously proposed as the perfect design solution
sentences.zh: 但在大约100年的时间里，轻于空气的飞行器曾被认真提议为解决各种问题的完美设计方案，

sentences.en: for all kinds of problems, even though none of these proposals actually happened.
sentences.zh: 尽管这些提议最终无一真正实现。

sentences.en: People just couldn't give up on the promise of airships.
sentences.zh: 人们就是无法放弃对飞艇的憧憬。

sentences.en: In the 90s, there was a company called Sky Station.
sentences.zh: 在90年代，有一家名为“天空之站”的公司。

sentences.en: They raised some $4.2 billion, or at least solicited it,
sentences.zh: 他们筹集了大约42亿美元，或者至少是寻求了这么多资金，

sentences.en: to put 250 antenna-equipped airships to deliver internet service.
sentences.zh: 计划部署250艘配备天线的飞艇来提供互联网服务。

sentences.en: This is Bill Hammack.
sentences.zh: 这位是比尔·哈马克。

sentences.en: He's the engineer guy on YouTube and an airship enthusiaSt.
sentences.zh: 他是油管上的工程师老哥，也是一位飞艇狂热爱好者。

sentences.en: In the 80s, there was the British Antarctic Survey.
sentences.zh: 在80年代，英国南极调查局行动了。

sentences.en: They revealed a hole in the ozone layer over the South Pole.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了南极上空的臭氧层空洞。

sentences.en: And so pretty soon, a professor suggested sending blimps that dangled electrical wires
sentences.zh: 因此没过多久，一位教授建议派遣悬挂电线的气艇，

sentences.en: to zap ozone-eating chemicals.
sentences.zh: 去消灭那些吞噬臭氧的化学物质。

sentences.en: Then in the 70s, they were supposed to help developing nations.
sentences.zh: 而在70年代，它们本应去帮助发展中国家。

sentences.en: Using a hybrid blimp to usher those nations into the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 利用混合动力飞艇将这些国家带入20世纪。

sentences.en: No need for roads, no need for railroads and tunnels and bridges, but just to lift stuff in.
sentences.zh: 不需要公路，不需要铁路、隧道和桥梁，只需要把东西吊运进去。

sentences.en: In the 1950s and 60s, nuclear-powered airships with unlimited energy
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50和60年代，人们曾提议建造拥有无限能源

sentences.en: and an unlimited capacity for work were proposed.
sentences.zh: 以及无限工作能力的核动力飞艇。

sentences.en: In the 20s and 30s, they were to fulfill imperial ambitions.
sentences.zh: 在20和30年代，它们是为了实现帝国的野心。

sentences.en: Both Germany and the British were looking for that.
sentences.zh: 德国和英国都在寻求这一点。

sentences.en: And the Americans, too.
sentences.zh: 美国人也是如此。

sentences.en: They had imperial ambitions in the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 他们在菲律宾有着帝国的野心。

sentences.en: Of all those failed attempts to realize the full potential of airships,
sentences.zh: 在所有未能实现飞艇全部潜力的失败尝试中，

sentences.en: it was those imperial rigid airships, heavily developed in the 20s and 30s,
sentences.zh: 正是那些在20和30年代大力发展、具有帝国色彩的硬式飞艇，

sentences.en: that came the closest to actually changing the world.
sentences.zh: 最接近真正改变世界。

sentences.en: In an airship, you have a metal framework, and that houses gas bags that lift the ship.
sentences.zh: 在一艘飞艇中，你有一个金属骨架，它容纳着让飞艇升空的气囊。

sentences.en: Those gas bags are arranged in the metal scaffolding, like peas in a peapod.
sentences.zh: 这些气囊像豆荚里的豌豆一样排列在金属支架中。

sentences.en: And then a cloth cover is stretched over that, and that cloth cover is not airtight.
sentences.zh: 然后外面绷上一层布罩，这层布罩并不气密。

sentences.en: It protects the gas bags from weather.
sentences.zh: 它保护气囊免受风雨侵袭。

sentences.en: Underneath the fabric cover are not just gas bags.
sentences.zh: 织物罩下方不仅仅只有气囊。

sentences.en: Because it's not a pressure vessel, they're able to build things inside the airship.
sentences.zh: 因为这不是一个压力容器，他们能够在飞艇内部建造各种设施。

sentences.en: Like crew quarters, dining rooms, lounges, all built into the metal framework.
sentences.zh: 比如船员舱、餐厅、休息室，全都内置在金属框架中。

sentences.en: So people move around inside the thing that you might think of as the balloon.
sentences.zh: 所以人们可以在你可能认为只是气球的物体内部四处走动。

sentences.en: But it's not really a balloon.
sentences.zh: 但它其实并不是气球。

sentences.en: And that structure enables an airship to travel faster than a blimp,
sentences.zh: 这种结构使飞艇能够比软式飞艇飞得更快，

sentences.en: because the force of the wind, for example, would deform the nose of a blimp.
sentences.zh: 因为例如风力会使软式飞艇的艇头变形。

sentences.en: And it also allows the ship to be built much, much bigger.
sentences.zh: 这也使得飞艇可以建造得非常巨大。

sentences.en: You've maybe heard the term dirigible, which is the French name for an airship,
sentences.zh: 你可能听过“双层飞艇”这个词，这是飞艇的法语名称，

sentences.en: or Zeppelin, which is a German company that makes airships.
sentences.zh: 或者“齐柏林”，这是一个制造飞艇的德国公司。

sentences.en: Zeppelin is like the Kleenex or Band-Aid of the airship world.
sentences.zh: 齐柏林就像是飞艇世界的“克林内克斯”或“邦迪创可贴”。

sentences.en: But the proper term, as generic and boring as it sounds, is airship.
sentences.zh: 但正确的术语，尽管听起来平淡无奇，就是飞艇。

sentences.en: The most promising, most opulent, rigid airship of its time,
sentences.zh: 那个时代最具前景、最奢华的硬式飞艇，

sentences.en: and I'm talking about the 1920s here, was Britain's R-101.
sentences.zh: 我这里指的是20世纪20年代，是英国的R-101。

sentences.en: The R there stands for rigid.
sentences.zh: 其中的R代表“硬式”。

sentences.en: The rise and dramatic fall of Britain's last great airship
sentences.zh: 英国最后一艘伟大飞艇的崛起与戏剧性陨落，

sentences.en: is the primary subject of Bill Hammock's new book called Fatal Flight.
sentences.zh: 是比尔·哈马克的新书《致命飞行》的主题。

sentences.en: Spoiler alert.
sentences.zh: 剧透警告。

sentences.en: When it comes to the dream of airships dominating the skies,
sentences.zh: 当谈到飞艇统治天空的梦想时，

sentences.en: the catastrophic and very public Hindenburg disaster
sentences.zh: 那场灾难性且备受瞩目的兴登堡空难

sentences.en: may have been the final nail in the coffin.
sentences.zh: 可能是棺材板上的最后一颗钉子。

sentences.en: But it was the crash of R-101 that built the coffin.
sentences.zh: 但真正造好这口棺材的，是R-101的坠毁。

sentences.en: R-101 was supposed to connect the global British Empire.
sentences.zh: R-101本应连接全球的大英帝国。

sentences.en: It was designed to fly from London to Karachi in five days.
sentences.zh: 它的设计是从伦敦飞往卡拉奇，耗时五天。

sentences.en: That's ten days faster than by sea.
sentences.zh: 这比走海路快了十天。

sentences.en: Taking a plane that distance took 16 days,
sentences.zh: 乘飞机走这段距离需要16天，

sentences.en: because planes had to stop so often to refuel.
sentences.zh: 因为飞机不得不频繁降落加油。

sentences.en: Airships could also carry 30 to 40 times the cargo of airplanes.
sentences.zh: 飞艇的载货量也可以达到飞机的30到40倍。

sentences.en: Airships just made so much sense for an empire whose reach exceeded its grasp.
sentences.zh: 对于一个雄心勃勃却力不从心的帝国来说，飞艇实在太合情合理了。

sentences.en: So Great Britain built R-101 and R-100,
sentences.zh: 于是大不列颠建造了R-101和R-100，

sentences.en: which was its sister ship that was supposed to go to Canada and back,
sentences.zh: 也就是它的姊妹舰，本应往返于加拿大，

sentences.en: as the first two rigid ships in a fleet
sentences.zh: 作为舰队中的前两艘硬式飞艇，

sentences.en: that would give the crown dominance over the skies
sentences.zh: 这支舰队将赋予英国王室对天空的统治地位，

sentences.en: to match its centuries-long dominance of the seas.
sentences.zh: 以匹配其几个世纪以来对海洋的统治地位。

sentences.en: An airship is conceptually quite simple,
sentences.zh: 飞艇在概念上相当简单，

sentences.en: but it's still an engineering marvel.
sentences.zh: 但它仍然是一个工程奇迹。

sentences.en: It's a gargantuan, cigar-shaped math equation,
sentences.zh: 它是一个巨大的、雪茄形的数学方程式，

sentences.en: balancing lift on one side of the equation and weight on the other.
sentences.zh: 方程式的一边平衡着升力，另一边平衡着重量。

sentences.en: Minimizing the weight of the airship was always a challenge.
sentences.zh: 尽量减轻飞艇的重量一直是一项挑战。

sentences.en: There's that rigid metal framework,
sentences.zh: 那里有那个硬式金属骨架，

sentences.en: and that is one of the most difficult parts,
sentences.zh: 这是最困难的部分之一，

sentences.en: because that has to be lightweight yet strong.
sentences.zh: 因为它必须既轻巧又坚固。

sentences.en: Yet R-101 was supposed to match the sturdy luxury of a high-end ocean liner.
sentences.zh: 然而R-101本应媲美高端远洋客轮的坚固奢华。

sentences.en: I mean, I can just picture this white china that was trimmed with royal blue
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我简直能想象出饰有皇家蓝色边的白瓷餐具，

sentences.en: and silver salt shakers and crystal glasses and small butter dishes.
sentences.zh: 还有银制盐瓶、水晶玻璃杯和小型黄油碟。

sentences.en: But to allow for those essential refinements,
sentences.zh: 但为了实现这些必不可少的精美细节，

sentences.en: everything else could only have the thinnest veneer of opulence,
sentences.zh: 其他所有东西都只能有一层极薄的奢华表象，

sentences.en: because they needed everything to weigh as little as possible.
sentences.zh: 因为他们需要一切东西都尽可能轻。

sentences.en: One person described it when they touched the ceiling as like a piece of staged scenery.
sentences.zh: 有人在触摸天花板时将其形容为像舞台布景一样。

sentences.en: All the walls were actually fabric.
sentences.zh: 所有的墙壁实际上都是织物。

sentences.en: The pillars in the lounge were made from balsa covered with metal.
sentences.zh: 休息室里的柱子是用覆有金属的轻木制成的。

sentences.en: The tables were also a balsa,
sentences.zh: 桌子也是轻木做的，

sentences.en: and the chairs were made of the lightest cane.
sentences.zh: 椅子则是由最轻的藤条制成。

sentences.en: So it was really kind of an illusion, the solidity of the ship,
sentences.zh: 所以这艘飞艇的坚固感其实有点像是一种幻觉，

sentences.en: because you just couldn't afford to lift, you know, tons and tons of stuff.
sentences.zh: 因为你根本负担不起去运送几吨又几吨的东西。

sentences.en: On the other side of the equation is lift.
sentences.zh: 方程式的另一边是升力。

sentences.en: You get lift from pumping in gas that's lighter than air.
sentences.zh: 你通过注入比空气轻的气体来获得升力。

sentences.en: In the case of R-101, the gas they used was hydrogen.
sentences.zh: 就R-101而言，他们使用的气体是氢气。

sentences.en: Well, flammable hydrogen seems like a very poor choice.
sentences.zh: 嗯，易燃的氢气听起来是个非常糟糕的选择。

sentences.en: It was, for a commercial airship, the only choice.
sentences.zh: 对商业飞艇而言，它是唯一的选择。

sentences.en: You used hydrogen instead of helium, which is non-flammable,
sentences.zh: 你使用氢气而不是不可燃的氦气，

sentences.en: because the purpose of a ship like R-101 was to transport cargo.
sentences.zh: 因为像R-101这样的飞艇的目的是运载货物。

sentences.en: And helium is both heavier and provides less lift than hydrogen.
sentences.zh: 而且氦气比氢气重，提供的升力也比氢气少。

sentences.en: What you're interested in is the payload that you can lift.
sentences.zh: 你所关心的是你能举起的载荷。

sentences.en: So if you subtract all of the weight that you have to lift,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你减去你必须抬升的所有重量，

sentences.en: the rigid ship, the gas bags, the water, the personnel,
sentences.zh: 硬式飞艇、气囊、水、人员，

sentences.en: in a ship like R-101, if you filled it with helium,
sentences.zh: 在像R-101这样的飞艇中，如果你给它充入氦气，

sentences.en: you would not have enough lift to lift the ship.
sentences.zh: 你就没有足够的升力来让飞艇升空。

sentences.en: The flammability of hydrogen was indeed a concern in airships.
sentences.zh: 氢气的易燃性确实是飞艇的一个隐患。

sentences.en: But flight engineers and crew were habituated to its dangers,
sentences.zh: 但飞行工程师和机组人员已经习惯了它的危险，

sentences.en: much like we're habituated to the dangers of combustion engines today.
sentences.zh: 就像我们今天习惯内燃机的危险一样。

sentences.en: They felt that you just take the proper precautions.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得只要采取适当的防范措施就行了。

sentences.en: One engineer pointed out you don't light a match and look in your gas tank in your car
sentences.zh: 一位工程师指出，当你现在开着时刻携带高度易燃物的汽车时，

sentences.en: when you're driving around with something highly flammable all of the time right now.
sentences.zh: 你不会点燃火柴去汽车油箱里查看。

sentences.en: You get the proper engineering solutions and controls to do it.
sentences.zh: 你会采用恰当的工程解决方案和控制措施来做到这一点。

sentences.en: The other reason why helium wasn't an option on commercial airships was the coSt.
sentences.zh: 商业飞艇不考虑氦气的另一个原因是成本。

sentences.en: Helium at that time was produced in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当时的氦气产自美国。

sentences.en: It comes from natural gas that's required expensive distillation plants,
sentences.zh: 它来自需要昂贵蒸馏设备的天然气，

sentences.en: and most of the helium is in places like Kansas and Oklahoma and Texas.
sentences.zh: 而且大部分氦气都在堪萨斯州、俄克拉荷马州和得克萨斯州等地。

sentences.en: So they would have to pay for it to be imported into Britain.
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须支付将其进口到英国的费用。

sentences.en: Instead, you can make hydrogen on-site very cheaply.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，你可以在现场非常廉价地制造氢气。

sentences.en: Almost one-one-hundredth of the cost of helium.
sentences.zh: 成本几乎不到氦气的一百分之一。

sentences.en: So that was never really, you know, an option, never really considered.
sentences.zh: 所以这从来都不是一个真正的选项，从未被认真考虑过。

sentences.en: The gas bags that contain the hydrogen are their own engineering marvel.
sentences.zh: 盛放氢气的气囊本身就是个工程奇迹。

sentences.en: It's interesting to me as an engineer to think about the materials they had to make these gas bags,
sentences.zh: 作为一名工程师，想到他们用来制作这些气囊的材料，我感到很有意思，

sentences.en: because you have a problem in that hydrogen wants to permeate.
sentences.zh: 因为你面临一个问题，那就是氢气具有渗透性。

sentences.en: It's a small molecule.
sentences.zh: 它是一种小分子。

sentences.en: It likes to go through things.
sentences.zh: 它喜欢穿透各种东西。

sentences.en: So you need something that's very strong, that is impermeable to hydrogen, or largely impermeable,
sentences.zh: 所以你需要一种非常坚固、对氢气不渗透（或基本不渗透）且轻质的材料。

sentences.en: and that is lightweight.
sentences.zh: 因此他们尝试了橡胶、明胶、甘油以及一种叫做粘胶纤维的东西，

sentences.en: And so they tried things like rubber, gelatin, glycerin, something called viscose,
sentences.zh: 这是一种合成织物。

sentences.en: which is a synthetic fabric.
sentences.zh: 它涂有乳胶。

sentences.en: It's coated with latex.
sentences.zh: 但它们都以这样或那样的方式失败了。

sentences.en: But they all failed one way or another.
sentences.zh: 比如粘胶纤维，如果你把它揉成团，就无法再把它展开。

sentences.en: Like the viscose, if you crumpled it up, you could not uncrumple.
sentences.zh: 它会直接裂开。

sentences.en: It would just crack.
sentences.zh: 所以他们使用了一种直到今天都让我大吃一惊的材料——牛的肠子。

sentences.en: So they used, and this stuns me to this day, the intestines of an oxen.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，牛的肠子里有一层非常细的膜。

sentences.en: And specifically, the oxen intestine, it's lined with a very fine membrane.
sentences.zh: 它被称为盲肠。

sentences.en: It's called the cecum.
sentences.zh: 它非常薄且具有柔韧性。

sentences.en: And it's very thin and flexible.
sentences.zh: 氢气只能缓慢地通过它渗漏。

sentences.en: And hydrogen seeps only slowly through it.
sentences.zh: 牛肠几乎是完美的材料，除了尺寸问题。

sentences.en: Ox intestines are nearly the perfect material, except for the size.
sentences.zh: 一头牛的盲肠大约是30英寸乘6英寸，也就是略多于一平方英尺。

sentences.en: The cecum of an ox is about 30 inches by 6 inches, so a little over a square foot.
sentences.zh: 然而其中一个气囊如果铺展开来，有30000平方英尺。

sentences.en: And yet one of those gas bags, if you laid it out, is 30,000 square feet.
sentences.zh: 因此，要制造其中一个气囊，你需要用到大约50000个这样的动物内脏。

sentences.en: And so to create one of these gas bags, you would use 50,000 of these entrails or so.
sentences.zh: 事实上，建造R101所需的15个气囊，

sentences.en: In fact, there's over a million and a half oxen intestines that were needed
sentences.zh: 总共需要超过一百五十万个牛肠。

sentences.en: to create the 15 gas bags for R101.
sentences.zh: 结束

sentences.en: And it was fairly grisly work.
sentences.zh: 这确实是相当骇人的工作。

sentences.en: They delivered from slaughterhouses in Argentina, at least some of the animals,
sentences.zh: 它们运自阿根廷的屠宰场，至少其中一些动物是这样的，

sentences.en: barrels of these guts.
sentences.zh: 装着这些内脏的桶。

sentences.en: And then they would scrape them and go through this long process to prepare them
sentences.zh: 然后他们会把它们刮干净，经历漫长的工序来处理它们，

sentences.en: and eventually to glue them together.
sentences.zh: 最后把它们粘合在一起。

sentences.en: And to answer your question, 50,000 oxen intestines,
sentences.zh: 顺便回答你的问题，五万根牛的肠子，

sentences.en: even once cured and treated to make them into gas bags, do kind of stink.
sentences.zh: 即使经过固化和处理做成气囊，其实还是会有点臭。

sentences.en: They did.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: They did.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Apparently, if you were up in the airship, you would smell, you know,
sentences.zh: 显然，如果你在飞艇上，你会闻到，你知道的，

sentences.en: kind of an animal smell, a musky smell also, because the cloth cover didn't allow light in.
sentences.zh: 一种动物的气味，还有一种麝香味，因为布质外罩不透光。

sentences.en: R101 had a few test flights in and around its hangar outside London to great fanfare.
sentences.zh: R101在伦敦郊外的机库及其周边进行了几次试飞，伴随着巨大的欢呼声。

sentences.en: In fact, Bill Hammock surmises that the focus on PR and fanfare,
sentences.zh: 事实上，比尔·汉莫克推测，对公关和造势的关注，

sentences.en: rather than more rigorous and deliberative testing,
sentences.zh: 而不是更严格、更审慎的测试，

sentences.en: led to the tragedy that was about to come on the ship's first attempted flight to India in 1930.
sentences.zh: 导致了这艘飞艇在1930年首次飞往印度的尝试中即将发生的悲剧。

sentences.en: It had left on October 4th, about 6.30 at night.
sentences.zh: 它于10月4日晚上6点半左右出发。

sentences.en: About 54 people on board.
sentences.zh: 船上大约有54人。

sentences.en: Most of them worked for the Royal Airship Works, but some were observers and some were dignitaries.
sentences.zh: 他们大多为英国皇家飞艇厂工作，但也有一些是观察员和政要。

sentences.en: So it traveled across England, it traveled across the channel into France,
sentences.zh: 于是它飞越了英格兰，飞越海峡进入法国，

sentences.en: and there were these bruising winds.
sentences.zh: 那里刮起了强烈的乱风。

sentences.en: It was just winds so fierce that ground speed was only 30 miles per hour or so.
sentences.zh: 风实在太猛烈了，地速只有每小时30英里左右。

sentences.en: And then a few minutes past two, it was about 40 miles or 64 kilometers north of Paris,
sentences.zh: 接着在过两点几分钟的时候，它在巴黎以北大约40英里或64公里处，

sentences.en: and it kind of chopped through the turbulent air, flying at about 1,200 feet,
sentences.zh: 它在约1200英尺的高度穿过湍流，

sentences.en: but moving up and down a couple of hundred feet.
sentences.zh: 上下起伏了有两百英尺左右。

sentences.en: And the top cover ripped open.
sentences.zh: 然后顶部外罩被撕裂了。

sentences.en: The top cover was weak.
sentences.zh: 顶部外罩很脆弱。

sentences.en: It was one of the weakest parts of the ship.
sentences.zh: 它是飞艇最薄弱的部位之一。

sentences.en: Then at that point, the gas bags, which are made of these very thin intestines, were exposed to rain.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，由这些极薄的肠子制成的气囊暴露在了雨中。

sentences.en: The rain pelted the gas bags.
sentences.zh: 雨水猛烈打在气囊上。

sentences.en: There was some decrease in lift, maybe drop to 500 feet or so.
sentences.zh: 升力有所下降，可能降到了500英尺左右。

sentences.en: And the control car, and no one knows why today, signaled for the engine power to be cut off.
sentences.zh: 而控制舱——至今无人知晓原因——发出了切断发动机动力的信号。

sentences.en: And of course, it lost all dynamic lift at that point.
sentences.zh: 当然，它在那一刻失去了所有的动升力。

sentences.en: And it drove nose first to the ground.
sentences.zh: 并且机头朝下冲向地面。

sentences.en: It slid into a grove of hazel and oak trees, and it burst into flame.
sentences.zh: 它滑进了一片榛树和橡树林，并轰然起火。

sentences.en: There's some debate as to why it burst into flames.
sentences.zh: 关于它为什么会起火，还有一些争论。

sentences.en: Bill Hammack thinks the fire might have been caused by calcium-phosphide flares that were kept in the control car.
sentences.zh: 比尔·汉莫克认为，大火可能是由存放在控制舱内的磷化钙信号弹引起的。

sentences.en: Those ignite when water hits them.
sentences.zh: 那些东西一遇到水就会点燃。

sentences.en: And of course, that ignited the hydrogen.
sentences.zh: 当然，这引燃了氢气。

sentences.en: At that point, just everything became charred.
sentences.zh: 到了那个时候，一切都烧焦了。

sentences.en: Only six people survived it.
sentences.zh: 只有六个人幸存。

sentences.en: The ground was littered with these, you know, very sad everyday things.
sentences.zh: 地面上散落着这些，你知道的，非常悲伤的日常用品。

sentences.en: I mean, suitcases, fur-lined boots, shard-shaving brushes, ten of cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 我是说，手提箱、带毛皮内衬的靴子、碎掉的剃须刷、几十支香烟。

sentences.en: I think there was a ticking watch still there.
sentences.zh: 我想那里还有一块滴答作响的手表。

sentences.en: And tens of plums with its juice leaking.
sentences.zh: 还有几十个李子，汁水正流淌出来。

sentences.en: And then it was very quiet.
sentences.zh: 然后四周变得非常安静。

sentences.en: And all you could hear was the hiss of the rain as it hit the hot metal and it evaporated.
sentences.zh: 你只能听到雨水击打在炽热金属上并蒸发时的嘶嘶声。

sentences.en: The wreckage had barely cooled when the British government halted their airship program for good.
sentences.zh: 残骸甚至还没冷却，英国政府就彻底叫停了他们的飞艇计划。

sentences.en: It was almost immediate.
sentences.zh: 几乎是立刻决定的。

sentences.en: R-100 had flown to Montreal and back, and it was in a shed, and it never flew again.
sentences.zh: R-100曾飞往蒙特利尔并返回，它当时停在机库里，但再也没有飞过。

sentences.en: They eventually steamrolled R-100, sold some of the parts for scrap, sold some to people who wanted souvenirs.
sentences.zh: 他们最终用蒸汽压路机碾毁了R-100，把一些零件当废品卖了，还卖给了一些想要纪念品的人。

sentences.en: Even though R-101 was completely destroyed in the French countryside,
sentences.zh: 尽管R-101在法国乡间彻底损毁，

sentences.en: the burned remains did float in the sky once again, at least for a little while.
sentences.zh: 烧毁的残骸却再次漂浮在天空中，至少持续了一小会儿。

sentences.en: Well, the wreckage of that ship was cut up into pieces, shipped back in December to Great Britain,
sentences.zh: 好吧，那艘飞艇的残骸被切成碎片，在12月运回英国，

sentences.en: and it went to somebody who takes scrap metal.
sentences.zh: 交给了一个回收废金属的人。

sentences.en: And then, apparently, according to a newspaper account, it was sold to the Zeppelin Company,
sentences.zh: 然后，根据报纸记载，它显然被卖给了齐柏林公司，

sentences.en: and they used part of that metal to make the Hindenburg.
sentences.zh: 他们用部分金属制造了兴登堡号。

sentences.en: Because of the romanticism wrapped up in airships, their flexibility when it comes to moving huge cargo,
sentences.zh: 由于人们对飞艇抱有的浪漫主义情怀、它们在运送巨型货物时的灵活性，

sentences.en: and the fact that it requires very little infrastructure to support their operation,
sentences.zh: 以及它们运营所需的基础设施非常少这一事实，

sentences.en: the hope that airships will make a return has never gone away.
sentences.zh: 飞艇东山再起的希望从未破灭。

sentences.en: I mean, I get the question a lot, you know, are airships going to come back and with new materials?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我经常被问到这个问题，你知道的，飞艇会卷土重来吗，还会用上新材料吗？

sentences.en: Part of the reason why they don't come back is this fiery, disaster-filled legacy, which I am perpetuating right now.
sentences.zh: 它们没有卷土重来的部分原因，就是这段充满了火灾与灾难的历史，而我正在不断重提这段历史。

sentences.en: What politician wants to vote in an airship and have it crash?
sentences.zh: 哪个政治家愿意投票支持建造飞艇却眼睁睁看着它坠毁呢？

sentences.en: And somebody said, well, you know, didn't you know about the Hindenburg, right?
sentences.zh: 有人说，好吧，你知道的，难道你们不知道兴登堡号吗？

sentences.en: Now, I would note, this isn't quite fair.
sentences.zh: 现在，我要指出的是，这并不完全公平。

sentences.en: If you look at something like the Graf Zeppelin, which was a contemporary of R-101 and a predecessor to the Hindenburg,
sentences.zh: 如果你看看像齐柏林伯爵号这样的飞艇——它是R-101的同时代产品，也是兴登堡号的前身——

sentences.en: it was in service for nine years, it crossed the Atlantic 144 times, 16,000 flight hours, 590 flights, 13,000 passengers,
sentences.zh: 它服役了九年，横跨大西洋144次，飞行时间16,000小时，飞行590架次，搭载乘客13,000人，

sentences.en: the first aircraft ever to exceed one million flight miles, and circumnavigated the globe in just 21 days.
sentences.zh: 它是第一款飞行里程超过一百万英里的飞行器，并在短短21天内完成了环球航行。

sentences.en: So there is, you know, another history back there that says that these things can be made and can be made well.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，还有另一段历史表明，这些东西是可以制造出来的，而且可以造得很好。

sentences.en: At this point, the airplane has had a century's worth of development in efficiency, speed, and safety,
sentences.zh: 时至今日，飞机在效率、速度和安全性方面已经经历了一个世纪的发展，

sentences.en: so that the need for the airship has been largely eliminated.
sentences.zh: 以至于对飞艇的需求在很大程度上已经消失了。

sentences.en: But a past is precedent.
sentences.zh: 但过去就是先例。

sentences.en: Some enterprising engineer is in a room full of venture capitalists right now,
sentences.zh: 某个富有进取心的工程师此刻正坐在一间挤满风险投资家的屋子里，

sentences.en: trying to convince them that giant airships are the solution to some pressing world problem.
sentences.zh: 试图说服他们巨型飞艇是解决某些紧迫世界问题的方案。

sentences.en: In the meantime, the airship will continue on in science fiction stories as this quick and easy visual cue
sentences.zh: 与此同时，飞艇将继续存在于科幻小说中，作为一个迅速而简便的视觉符号，

sentences.en: that we're in a world that's like ours, but somehow more wondrous.
sentences.zh: 向我们暗示我们身处一个类似于我们的世界，但却更加奇妙。

sentences.en: One of the most memorable pieces of audio of all time and my favorite video by the engineer guy, right after this.
sentences.zh: 史上最难忘的音频片段之一，也是我最喜欢的“工程师”频道的视频，广告回来马上揭晓。

sentences.en: When the Hindenburg crashed and burned in a New Jersey field in 1937,
sentences.zh: 1937年，当兴登堡号在新泽西州的一片田野里坠毁并起火时，

sentences.en: a reporter from Chicago radio station WLS named Herbert Morrison was there.
sentences.zh: 来自芝加哥WLS广播电台的记者赫伯特·莫里森就在现场。

sentences.en: His real-time reaction to the disaster that was unfolding in front of him
sentences.zh: 他对眼前正在上演的灾难所做出的实时反应，

sentences.en: became one of the most memorable recordings in broadcast history.
sentences.zh: 成为了广播史上最难忘的录音之一。

sentences.en: A couple people on staff here had never heard it before, which totally shocked me,
sentences.zh: 我们这里的几位工作人员以前从未听过，这让我大为震惊，

sentences.en: so I wanted to play it here.
sentences.zh: 所以我今天想在这里播放一下。

sentences.en: You might not be able to make out all the words, but Morrison's emotions come through loud and clear.
sentences.zh: 你可能听不清所有的词，但莫里森的情感却清晰而强烈地传达了出来。

sentences.en: It's starting to rain again.
sentences.zh: 又开始下雨了。

sentences.en: The rain had slacked up a little bit.
sentences.zh: 雨势刚刚减小了一点。

sentences.en: The back motors of the ship are just holding it just enough to keep it from...
sentences.zh: 飞艇后面的发动机正勉强支撑着它，不让它……

sentences.en: It's bursting into flames.
sentences.zh: 它起火了。

sentences.en: Get this, Charlie.
sentences.zh: 看这个，查理。

sentences.en: Get this, Charlie.
sentences.zh: 看这个，查理。

sentences.en: It's rising.
sentences.zh: 它在上升。

sentences.en: It's rising.
sentences.zh: 它在上升。

sentences.en: It's rising.
sentences.zh: 它在上升。

sentences.en: Terrible.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: Oh, my.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Get out of the way, please.
sentences.zh: 请让开，拜托。

sentences.en: It's burning, bursting into flames, and it's falling on the morning grass,
sentences.zh: 它在燃烧，燃起大火，正坠落在早晨的草地上，

sentences.en: and all the folks between us, this is terrible.
sentences.zh: 我们之间的所有人，这太可怕了。

sentences.en: This is one of the worst catastrophes in the world.
sentences.zh: 这是世界上最严重的灾难之一。

sentences.en: Oh, it's like twenty, oh, four or five hundred feet into the sky,
sentences.zh: 哦，它大概升到了天空两千、哦，四五百英尺的高度，

sentences.en: and it's a terrific crash, ladies and gentlemen.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，这是一场可怕的坠毁。

sentences.en: It's smoking, it's flames now, and the flame is rising to the ground,
sentences.zh: 它在冒烟，现在有火焰了，火焰正在向地面蔓延，

sentences.en: not quite to the morning grass.
sentences.zh: 还没完全触及早晨的草地。

sentences.en: Oh, the humanity and all the fans are just screaming around here.
sentences.zh: 哦，人类啊，所有歌迷都在周围尖叫。

sentences.en: I don't...
sentences.zh: 我不能……

sentences.en: I can't talk to people around there.
sentences.zh: 我无法和周围的人说话。

sentences.en: I can't talk, ladies and gentlemen.
sentences.zh: 我开不了口，女士们先生们。

sentences.en: Honestly, it's just laying down massive smoking wreckage,
sentences.zh: 说实话，它留下一片冒烟的巨大残骸，

sentences.en: and everybody can hardly breathe and talk and screaming.
sentences.zh: 每个人都几乎无法呼吸、无法说话，只能尖叫。

sentences.en: Lady, I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 女士，我很抱歉。

sentences.en: Honestly, I can hardly breathe.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我几乎喘不过气来。

sentences.en: I'm going to step inside while I cannot see it.
sentences.zh: 我要走进里面去，趁我还看不见它。

sentences.en: Charlie, that's terrible.
sentences.zh: 查理，这太可怕了。

sentences.en: I can't...
sentences.zh: 我不能……

sentences.en: Listen, folks, I'm going to have to stop for a minute
sentences.zh: 听着，各位，我得停下一会儿，

sentences.en: because I have lots of voices in the worst thing I've ever witnessed.
sentences.zh: 因为我听到了许多声音，这是我亲眼目睹过最糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: That radio recording was later paired with newsreel footage of the disaster.
sentences.zh: 这段广播录音后来与该灾难的新闻片镜头剪辑在了一起。

sentences.en: Thirty-six of the 97 people on board the Hindenburg died.
sentences.zh: 兴登堡号上的97人中有36人遇难。

sentences.en: When you see the footage of the burning airship,
sentences.zh: 当你看到燃烧飞艇的镜头时，

sentences.en: the fact that 61 people survived seems like a miracle.
sentences.zh: 61人幸存的事实简直就像一个奇迹。

sentences.en: As I mentioned in my introduction to Bill Hammock,
sentences.zh: 正如我在介绍比尔·汉莫克时所提到的，

sentences.en: on YouTube he's known as Engineer Guy,
sentences.zh: 他在YouTube上被称为“工程师” (Engineer Guy)，

sentences.en: and I would be remiss if I didn't point you toward his fantastic video
sentences.zh: 如果我不向大家推荐他那部关于铝制饮料罐精妙设计的精彩视频，

sentences.en: on the ingenious design of the aluminum beverage can,
sentences.zh: 我就会失职了。

sentences.en: which is, for my money, the greatest video on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，那是YouTube上最棒的视频。

sentences.en: It is 11 and a half minutes of everyday design and engineering glory.
sentences.zh: 那是长达十一分半钟的日常设计与工程荣耀。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: Here's a little audio sample.
sentences.zh: 这里有一小段音频样本。

sentences.en: Why is there a tab on the end of the can?
sentences.zh: 为什么罐子末端有一个拉环？

sentences.en: It seems a silly question.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个愚蠢的问题。

sentences.en: How else would you open it?
sentences.zh: 不然你还能怎么打开它？

sentences.en: But originally cans didn't have tabs.
sentences.zh: 但最初的罐子是没有拉环的。

sentences.en: Very early steel cans were called flat tops for pretty obvious reasons.
sentences.zh: 非常早期的钢罐被称为“平顶罐”，原因显而易见。

sentences.en: You use a special opener to puncture a hole to drink from
sentences.zh: 你用专用的开罐器扎出一个洞来喝饮料，

sentences.en: and a hole to vent.
sentences.zh: 再扎一个洞来通风。

sentences.en: In the 1960s, the pole tab was invented so that no opener was needed.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪60年代，人们发明了拉环，这样就不需要开罐器了。

sentences.en: You can find links to Bill's videos and his book on the R101 on his website,
sentences.zh: 你可以在他的网站上找到比尔的视频以及他关于R101的书籍链接，

sentences.en: engineerguy.com.
sentences.zh: engineerguy.com.

sentences.en: 99% Invisible is Avery Truffleman, Emmett Fitzgerald, Sharif Youssef,
sentences.zh: “99%隐形”节目组包括埃弗里·特拉夫曼 (Avery Truffleman)、埃米特·菲茨杰拉德 (Emmett Fitzgerald)、谢里夫·尤素夫 (Sharif Youssef)，

sentences.en: Taryn Maza, composer Sean Rial, digital director Kurt Kolstad,
sentences.zh: 塔琳·马扎 (Taryn Maza)、作曲家肖恩·里亚尔 (Sean Rial)、数字总监库尔特·科尔斯特ッド (Kurt Kolstad)，

sentences.en: senior editor Delaney Hall, senior producer Katie Mingle, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 资深编辑德兰妮·霍尔 (Delaney Hall)、资深制作人凯蒂·明格尔 (Katie Mingle)，以及我，罗曼·马尔斯 (Roman Mars)。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 KALW in San Francisco
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山91.7 KALW电台的项目，

sentences.en: and produced on Radio Row in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 制作于加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心美丽的广播街 (Radio Row)。

sentences.en: We are part of Radiotopia from PRX,
sentences.zh: 我们是PRX广播乌托邦 (Radiotopia) 的一部分，

sentences.en: a collective of the best, most innovative shows in all of podcasting.
sentences.zh: 这是一个汇集了整个播客界最好、最具创新性节目的联盟。

sentences.en: We are supported by our listeners, just like you.
sentences.zh: 我们由像你这样的听众资助。

sentences.en: You can find 99% Invisible and join discussions about the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到“99%隐形”并参与有关节目的讨论。

sentences.en: You can tweet at me at Roman Mars and the show at 99PI.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Twitter上向我@Roman Mars以及向节目组@99PI.org发送推文。

sentences.en: We're on Instagram, Tumblr, and Reddit too.
sentences.zh: 我们也在Instagram、Tumblr和Reddit上。

sentences.en: But we have very fun pictures and diagrams of airships on our website.
sentences.zh: 但我们的网站上有非常有趣的飞艇图片和图表。

sentences.en: They're even more amazing than you can picture in your head at 99PI.org.
sentences.zh: 它们比你脑海中想象的还要惊艳，网址是99PI.org。

sentences.zh: Radiotopia。
